Outside the exam hall Mridul held up the result sheet. "Binita, you lost marks on the whole probability section. You told me in September that it made no sense."

"I know."

"Then why didn't you ask the professor?"

"They would have thought I was weak. Everyone else seemed to follow. I kept telling myself I would work it out before the test."

"And now?"

Binita looked at the floor. "Now I have to go to the retest and I still don't understand the first chapter. I spent months worrying instead of asking, and it only got bigger." Mridul folded the sheet. "One question in September would have saved all that."

qa.a: Binita said the professor would have thought Binita was weak.

qa.q: What was Binita worried about when staying silent for months?
qa.a: Binita feared looking weak in front of the professor and the others, and hoped to work it out alone before the test.

qa.q: What could Binita try before the retest, and why would it help?
qa.a: Binita could bring a short list of the parts that make no sense to the professor, because a clear question shows effort and gets a direct answer.

qa.a: Mridul seems worried and a little frustrated, having watched Binita lose marks that one question might have saved.

passage:
I'm Gopika, and in my first semester of engineering I didn't ask a single question. Not one.
Professor Iyer taught signals, and from week three I was lost. Fourier series looked like a foreign alphabet. Every class I thought: if I ask, he'll decide I don't belong here. Everyone else was nodding. My classmate Gautam went to office hours every week, and I thought, he must be the slow one.
By week eight, my notes were full of question marks. I copied problem solutions without understanding them. The night before the exam, I tried to learn five weeks of material from videos and panicked.
I got 31 out of 100. Gautam got 78. Afterwards he told me half his office-hour questions were 'really basic', and Professor Iyer had never once made him feel stupid.
I'd been protecting my pride, and it cost me more than any question could have.

qa.q: What did Gopika score in the exam?
What was Gopika afraid of in class?
qa.a: Gopika felt afraid that asking would make the professor decide Gopika did not belong there, so stayed silent while feeling lost.

qa.q: What could Gopika have done in week three?
qa.a: Go to office hours with one small question, as Gautam did, before the confusion piled up.

qa.q: How might Professor Iyer see a silent student who fails?
qa.a: Professor Iyer may be surprised and sorry, since he welcomed basic questions and never had a chance to help.

grounding: Shows a student staying silent for fear of seeming weak, letting confusion grow until the exam, and scoring far lower than a classmate who asked.

Note to self, after mid-semester marking – R. Nair
Sunaina, second row, never asks questions. She takes careful notes and nods. I assumed she was following.
Her paper says otherwise. She got the first two questions right and left the last three blank, all on recursion, which we covered in weeks four to six. In the margin of question four she had written, very small, 'don't understand the stack'.
I asked her to stay after class today. She said she'd been confused since week four but didn't want me to think she was weak, especially since the class moves fast. She was close to tears.
That confusion could have been fixed in ten minutes in week four. Now she has lost marks she didn't need to lose.
I've given her a slot on Friday at 4, and tomorrow I'll tell the class that basic questions are welcome, at any time.

qa.q: What had Sunaina written in the margin of question four?
What was Sunaina feeling when asked to stay after class?
qa.a: She felt afraid of seeming weak and was close to tears, having hidden her confusion since week four.

qa.q: What could Sunaina bring to the Friday slot?
qa.a: Her attempts at the recursion questions, marked where the stack stops making sense, so the gap can be found fast.

qa.q: How does the paper change R. Nair's view of Sunaina?
qa.a: R. Nair sees that nodding did not mean understanding and regrets not making room for basic questions sooner.

grounding: Shows a student who stays silent out of fear of looking weak, letting confusion grow until marks fall, seen through a teacher's note.
